```{r}
  mutate(hcsa_class = factor(replace_na(hcsa_class, "Not analysed"),
                             levels = c("Hot spot (99%)", "Hot spot (95%)",
                                        "Cold spot (95%)", "Cold spot (99%)",
                                        "Not significant", "Not analysed")))

tm_shape(hcsa_map_data) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "hcsa_class",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c("Hot spot (99%)" = "#b30000", "Hot spot (95%)" = "#fc8d59",
                 "Cold spot (95%)" = "#74a9cf", "Cold spot (99%)" = "#045a8d",
                 "Not significant" = "#eeeeee", "Not analysed" = "#ffffff")),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Gi* hot / cold spot (p < 0.05)",
                            position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
    col = "grey60", lwd = 0.2) +
  map_furniture() +
  tm_compass(type = "arrow", size = 2.5,
             position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, 100, 200), text.size = 0.6,
              position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
```

Red townships sit in neighbourhoods with far more events than the national average would suggest (hot spots); blue townships sit in neighbourhoods with far fewer (cold spots), and darker shades mean more certainty. There are 40 hot spots and 53 cold spots. Almost all of the most certain hot spots are in the Dry Zone, the heartland of the armed uprising against the military, in lower Sagaing, Mandalay and northern Magway, and this map agrees with the previous one wherever both find something. Cold spots cover the delta, Yangon, Nay Pyi Taw and the Wa and eastern Shan ceasefire areas, meaning only that few events were recorded there, not that people there are safe. Northern Shan and Rakhine, scenes of the biggest offensives since late 2023, are not hot spots here: that does not mean they were calm, since their fighting was packed into a few quarters and a total over almost five years dilutes it, as the maps over time below show.

::: stat-conclusion
**Statistical conclusions.** Gi\* finds `r sum(str_detect(hcsa$hcsa_class, "Hot"))` hot spots and `r sum(str_detect(hcsa$hcsa_class, "Cold"))` cold spots, matching LISA wherever both are significant. All but one of the `r sum(hcsa$hcsa_class == "Hot spot (99%)")` hot spots at 99% confidence lie in the Dry Zone core (12 in lower Sagaing, Singu in Mandalay, and Myaing, Yesagyo, Pakokku and Pauk in Magway), the Bamar heartland of the People's Defence Force uprising [@iiss2022dryzone]. The exception, Hlaingbwe (61 events), is also a LISA Low-High outlier: quiet itself, but inside the Kayin border corridor where the KNU briefly took Myawaddy in April 2024 [@csis2024myawaddy].

Cold spots cover the delta, Yangon, Nay Pyi Taw and the Wa and eastern Shan ceasefire areas. They show only that these areas record few events; reading them as firmer regime control or ceasefire coverage is plausible but beyond the data [@aljazeera2024sacm].

Northern Shan and Rakhine, scenes of the largest offensives since late 2023, are **not** hot spots over the full period (northern Shan appears only under the log transform, @sec-lmsa-robust). If their fighting was brief, a 57-month total would dilute it; @sec-ehsa tests this.
:::

## Robustness of the hot and cold spots {#sec-lmsa-robust}

Each statistic is re-run under three alternatives, each changing one assumption:

- **KNN with k = 6.** A different neighbour rule (D3).
- **Log transform.** Counts are replaced by log(1 + count), which limits extreme values (D1).
- **FDR.** Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p \< 0.05 across the 329 tests (D6).

```{r}
#| label: robustness-run
gi_class3   <- function(gi, p) case_when(p < 0.05 & gi > 0 ~ "Hot",
                                         p < 0.05 & gi < 0 ~ "Cold",
                                         TRUE ~ "Not significant")

g_knn6 <- run_gistar(mmr_an$conflict_n, nb_knn6)
g_log  <- run_gistar(log1p(mmr_an$conflict_n), nb_primary)
l_knn6 <- run_lisa(mmr_an$conflict_n, nb_knn6)
l_log  <- run_lisa(log1p(mmr_an$conflict_n), nb_primary)

robust <- tibble(
  TS_PCODE  = mmr_an$TS_PCODE, ST = mmr_an$ST, TS = mmr_an$TS,
  g_primary = gi_class3(hcsa$gi_star, hcsa$p_sim),
  g_knn6    = gi_class3(g_knn6$gi_star, g_knn6$p_sim),
  g_log     = gi_class3(g_log$gi_star, g_log$p_sim),
  g_fdr     = gi_class3(hcsa$gi_star, hcsa$p_fdr),
  l_primary = lisa$lisa_class,
  l_knn6    = classify_lisa(l_knn6$quadrant, l_knn6$p_ii_sim),
  l_log     = classify_lisa(l_log$quadrant, l_log$p_ii_sim),
  l_fdr     = classify_lisa(lisa$quadrant, lisa$p_fdr))

summarise_spec <- function(alt, prim, stat, spec) {
  tibble(statistic = stat, specification = spec,
         significant = sum(alt != "Not significant"),
         same_class_as_primary = paste0(round(100 * mean(alt == prim), 1), "%"),
         primary_significant_retained = paste0(
           sum(alt == prim & prim != "Not significant"), " of ",
           sum(prim != "Not significant")))
}

bind_rows(
  summarise_spec(robust$g_primary, robust$g_primary, "Gi*", "Primary (Queen, count)"),
  summarise_spec(robust$g_knn6, robust$g_primary, "Gi*", "KNN k = 6"),
  summarise_spec(robust$g_log,  robust$g_primary, "Gi*", "log(1 + count)"),
  summarise_spec(robust$g_fdr,  robust$g_primary, "Gi*", "FDR-adjusted"),
  summarise_spec(robust$l_primary, robust$l_primary, "LISA", "Primary (Queen, count)"),
  summarise_spec(robust$l_knn6, robust$l_primary, "LISA", "KNN k = 6"),
  summarise_spec(robust$l_log,  robust$l_primary, "LISA", "log(1 + count)"),
  summarise_spec(robust$l_fdr,  robust$l_primary, "LISA", "FDR-adjusted")) |>
  kable()
```

No township switches between hot and cold, or High-High and Low-Low, under any specification; disagreement is only between significant and not significant at cluster edges. The map counts, for each township, the Gi\* specifications in which it is significant.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-robust
#| fig-cap: "Robustness of Gi* hot and cold spots: number of the four specifications (primary; KNN k = 6; log(1 + count); FDR-adjusted) under which each township is significant at p < 0.05."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 8.5
robust <- robust |>
  mutate(n_hot  = rowSums(across(c(g_primary, g_knn6, g_log, g_fdr), ~ .x == "Hot")),
         n_cold = rowSums(across(c(g_primary, g_knn6, g_log, g_fdr), ~ .x == "Cold")),
         robustness = case_when(
           n_hot == 4  ~ "Hot in 4 of 4",
           n_hot >= 2  ~ "Hot in 2–3 of 4",
           n_hot == 1  ~ "Hot in 1 of 4",
           n_cold == 4 ~ "Cold in 4 of 4",
           n_cold >= 2 ~ "Cold in 2–3 of 4",
           n_cold == 1 ~ "Cold in 1 of 4",
           TRUE        ~ "Never significant"))

robust_map_data <- mmr_conflict |>
  select(TS_PCODE) |>
  left_join(select(robust, TS_PCODE, robustness), by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(robustness = factor(replace_na(robustness, "Not analysed"),
                             levels = c("Hot in 4 of 4", "Hot in 2–3 of 4", "Hot in 1 of 4",
                                        "Never significant",
                                        "Cold in 1 of 4", "Cold in 2–3 of 4", "Cold in 4 of 4",
                                        "Not analysed")))

tm_shape(robust_map_data) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "robustness",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c("Hot in 4 of 4" = "#b30000", "Hot in 2–3 of 4" = "#fc8d59",
                 "Hot in 1 of 4" = "#fdd49e", "Never significant" = "#eeeeee",
                 "Cold in 1 of 4" = "#d0d1e6", "Cold in 2–3 of 4" = "#74a9cf",
                 "Cold in 4 of 4" = "#045a8d", "Not analysed" = "#ffffff")),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Significant Gi* spot in ...",
                            position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
    col = "grey60", lwd = 0.2) +
  map_furniture() +
  tm_compass(type = "arrow", size = 2.5,
             position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, 100, 200), text.size = 0.6,
              position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
```

The hot and cold spot test was repeated four ways, each changing one assumption: which townships count as neighbours, how extreme counts are treated, and how strictly chance is ruled out. The shading shows how many of the four versions agree, with the darkest colours meaning all four. 17 townships are hot spots in all four, 16 of them in the Dry Zone, the most reliable result of the whole-period analysis; 26 are cold spots in all four, mostly in the Wa and eastern Shan hills. No township is hot in one version and cold in another, so the choices change how far a cluster stretches, never whether it is hot or cold. A paler township is not wrong, only less certain: several hot spots outside the Dry Zone, such as the group around Dawei and Myawaddy on the Thai border, pass only some versions, and the quarter-by-quarter analysis later shows that most of these have been hot for years, which strengthens the case that they are real.

```{r}
#| label: robust-counts
robust |> count(robustness) |> kable()
```

::: stat-conclusion
**Statistical conclusions.**

- **Hot under every specification.** `r sum(robust$n_hot == 4)` townships, `r sum(robust$n_hot == 4 & robust$ST %in% c("Sagaing", "Magway", "Mandalay"))` of them in the Dry Zone. This core is the most reliable LMSA result, independent of the neighbour rule, extreme values or multiple-testing control.
- **Peripheral hot spots are fragile.** Only Hlaingbwe survives all four outside the Dry Zone. The Tanintharyi group (Dawei, Thayetchaung, Yebyu) and Shwegyin fail FDR, and Myawaddy, Myeik and Pyinoolwin are hot under the primary specification only. FDR binds hardest: even Monywa, the highest count, fails it. These are *possible* hot spots for EHSA to corroborate.
- **Cold under every specification.** `r sum(robust$n_cold == 4)` townships, mostly the Wa and eastern Shan block. Delta and Yangon cold spots often lose significance under the log transform or FDR.
- **No contradictions.** Choices change the *extent* of clusters, never their direction.
:::

## Value added (Bonus): bivariate LISA, airstrikes and the rest of the war {#sec-bivariate}

LISA and Gi\* cannot show whether one *kind* of violence follows another. Airstrikes need no front line, so they could fall where neighbours see little other fighting. The bivariate Local Moran's I tests this within the LMSA family.

::: callout-tip
## Method card: bivariate Local Moran's I

- **Question.** Does a township with many airstrikes sit among neighbours with many *other* events (High-High), or apart from them (High-Low)? Do townships with few airstrikes have heavily fought neighbours (Low-High)?
- **Method.** $I_i = z_{x,i} \sum_j w_{ij} z_{y,j}$, with $x$ the standardised airstrike count in *i* and $y$ the standardised count of all other events. It is asymmetric: swapping $x$ and $y$ asks a different question. Quadrants as in LISA [@anselin1995; @bivand2018].
- **Null model.** Conditional permutation, 999 simulations, *i*'s airstrikes fixed; two-sided p-value.
- **Assumptions.** LISA's neighbours and weights. The variables must not overlap, so $y$ = `conflict_n - airstrike_n` (airstrikes are a sub-type of *Explosions/Remote violence*).
- **Edge handling.** As for LISA; Cocokyun excluded.
- **Threshold.** p \< 0.05 on the map, with the FDR count reported.
:::

::: callout-important
## Decision: what to compare airstrikes with

**Criteria.** (a) *No double counting:* $y$ excludes airstrikes. (b) *Question fit:* $y$ is the rest of the war, not a slice. (c) *Stability* across seeds and neighbour rules.

**Candidates.** Four versions of $y$ pass (a): all other events, battles only, violence against civilians only, and non-air explosions. Total conflict and *Explosions/Remote violence* fail, as both contain airstrikes. Whether the airstrike variable itself is clean is covered under sensitivity.
:::

```{r}
#| label: bv-setup
bv_in <- mmr_an |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(other_n    = conflict_n - airstrike_n,   # all other armed-conflict events
         nonair_erv = erv_n - airstrike_n)        # explosions other than airstrikes
stopifnot(all(bv_in$other_n >= 0), all(bv_in$nonair_erv >= 0))

lw_primary <- nb2listw(nb_primary, style = "W")

# Bivariate LISA: x in the township, y in its neighbours. Returns one row per township.
run_bv <- function(x, y, nb, nsim = 999, seed = 2025, alpha = 0.05) {
  lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W")
  r  <- localmoran_bv(x, y, lw, nsim = nsim, iseed = seed)
  zx <- as.numeric(scale(x))
  ly <- as.numeric(lag.listw(lw, as.numeric(scale(y))))
  quadrant <- case_when(zx >= 0 & ly >= 0 ~ "High-High", zx >= 0 & ly < 0 ~ "High-Low",
                        zx <  0 & ly >= 0 ~ "Low-High", TRUE ~ "Low-Low")
  p <- r[, "Pr(z != E(Ibvi)) Sim"]
  tibble(Ibvi = r[, "Ibvi"], p = p, quadrant = quadrant,
         bv_class = if_else(p < alpha, quadrant, "Not significant"))
}

pairings <- c(`All other events` = "other_n", `Battles only` = "battles_n",
              `Civilian violence only` = "vac_n", `Explosions other than airstrikes` = "nonair_erv")

imap_dfr(pairings, function(col, label) {
  b <- run_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in[[col]], nb_primary)
  tibble(`Other variable (y)` = label,
         `Spearman rho with airstrikes` = round(cor(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in[[col]], method = "spearman"), 2),
         `High-High` = sum(b$bv_class == "High-High"),
         `Low-Low` = sum(b$bv_class == "Low-Low"),
         `High-Low` = sum(b$bv_class == "High-Low"),
         `Low-High` = sum(b$bv_class == "Low-High"))
}) |> kable()
```

Every pairing is strongly correlated (Spearman 0.61 to 0.89), and none produces a High-Low outlier. Battles only gives the most Low-Low townships, being the narrowest variable with the most zeros.

::: decision
**Decision.** All other events, the broadest version of "does the air war follow the rest of the war?" and the only one covering every non-air type. Battles only, the narrowest reading of "ground fighting", is kept as a sensitivity run.
:::

```{r}
#| label: bv-primary
bv <- run_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in$other_n, nb_primary) |>
  mutate(TS_PCODE = bv_in$TS_PCODE, ST = bv_in$ST, TS = bv_in$TS,
         airstrike_n = bv_in$airstrike_n, other_n = bv_in$other_n,
         p_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))

# Global bivariate Moran's I (same null model, for context)
set.seed(2025)
bv_global <- moran_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in$other_n, lw_primary, nsim = 999)
tibble(statistic = "Global bivariate Moran's I",
       value = round(bv_global$t0, 3),
       `permutation p` = (sum(bv_global$t >= bv_global$t0) + 1) / (length(bv_global$t) + 1)) |>
  kable()

bv |> count(bv_class, name = "townships") |>
  mutate(survive_fdr = map_int(bv_class, \(k) sum(bv$bv_class == k & bv$p_bh < 0.05))) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-bivariate
#| fig-cap: "Bivariate LISA: airstrikes in each township against other armed-conflict events in its neighbours (Queen contiguity with island bridges, 999 permutations). Only townships significant at p < 0.05 are coloured; all others are shown as not significant. Cocokyun is excluded from local inference."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 8.5
bv_levels <- c("High-High", "High-Low", "Low-High", "Low-Low", "Not significant", "Not analysed")
bv_map_data <- mmr_conflict |>
  select(TS_PCODE) |>
  left_join(select(bv, TS_PCODE, bv_class), by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(bv_class = factor(replace_na(bv_class, "Not analysed"), levels = bv_levels))

tm_shape(bv_map_data) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "bv_class",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c("High-High" = "#d7301f", "High-Low" = "#fc8d59",
                 "Low-High" = "#9ecae1", "Low-Low" = "#2171b5",
                 "Not significant" = "#eeeeee", "Not analysed" = "#ffffff")),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Bivariate LISA (p < 0.05)",
                            position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
    col = "grey60", lwd = 0.2) +
  map_furniture() +
  tm_compass(type = "arrow", size = 2.5,
             position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, 100, 200), text.size = 0.6,
              position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
```

This map compares two things: air and drone strikes in each township, and all other fighting in the townships around it. Red means many strikes amid heavy fighting nearby, dark blue means few strikes amid little fighting, and grey means no clear pattern. Air power follows the ground war: 29 townships with many strikes sit among heavily fought neighbours, mostly in Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay, together receiving a third of all recorded strikes, while 47 quiet townships sit among quiet neighbours, 43 of them with no strikes at all. No township has many strikes while its surroundings are calm, so in the main fighting zones civilians face both ground combat and attack from the air. The map cannot say which causes which, only that strikes and other fighting happen in the same places; about 71% of strikes are by state forces and most of the rest by resistance groups, so it mixes both sides. The five pale-blue townships, with few strikes but heavy fighting nearby, are weak results worth watching rather than firm findings.

::: stat-conclusion
**Statistical conclusions.** Global bivariate Moran's I is `r round(bv_global$t0, 2)` (permutation p = `r format.pval((sum(bv_global$t >= bv_global$t0) + 1) / (length(bv_global$t) + 1))`): townships with many airstrikes tend to be surrounded by many other events. `r sum(bv$bv_class == "High-High")` townships are High-High (`r sum(bv$bv_class == "High-High" & bv$ST == "Sagaing")` in Sagaing, `r sum(bv$bv_class == "High-High" & bv$ST %in% c("Magway", "Mandalay"))` in Magway and Mandalay, a few in Tanintharyi, Kayin and Bago (East)), holding `r round(100 * sum(bv$airstrike_n[bv$bv_class == "High-High"]) / sum(bv$airstrike_n))`% of all airstrikes. `r sum(bv$bv_class == "Low-Low")` are Low-Low (mainly Yangon, the delta, Nay Pyi Taw and the Shan hills), `r sum(bv$bv_class == "Low-Low" & bv$airstrike_n == 0)` of them with no airstrikes. There is **no High-Low outlier**, and `r sum(bv$bv_class == "Low-High")` townships are Low-High. After FDR, `r sum(bv$bv_class == "High-High" & bv$p_bh < 0.05)` High-High, `r sum(bv$bv_class == "Low-Low" & bv$p_bh < 0.05)` Low-Low and `r sum(bv$bv_class == "Low-High" & bv$p_bh < 0.05)` Low-High townships survive.
:::

```{r}
#| label: bv-compare
# How much does the bivariate result add to the univariate LISA of conflict_n (@sec-lmsa)?
uni <- run_lisa(bv_in$conflict_n, nb_primary) |>
  mutate(uni_class = classify_lisa(quadrant, p_ii_sim), TS = bv_in$TS)

table(bivariate = bv$bv_class, univariate = uni$uni_class) |> kable()

bv |>
  filter(bv_class %in% c("High-Low", "Low-High")) |>
  mutate(univariate_LISA = uni$uni_class[match(TS_PCODE, bv_in$TS_PCODE)]) |>
  select(State = ST, Township = TS, airstrikes = airstrike_n,
         other_events = other_n, bivariate = bv_class, univariate_LISA) |>
  arrange(desc(other_events)) |>
  kable()
```

**What the bivariate view adds.** Every bivariate High-High and Low-Low township is already High-High or Low-Low in the univariate LISA, so the clusters add little to the map. What is new is that airstrikes are *not* spatially independent of the rest of the war: they follow it, and are absent where it is absent. The discordant townships carry the rest. Yebyu (Tanintharyi) and Mingin (Sagaing) are univariate High-High, yet airstrikes are only 5% and 7.5% of their events, against `r round(100 * sum(bv$airstrike_n) / sum(bv$airstrike_n + bv$other_n), 1)`% nationally. Hakha (Chin) is Low-High here but not significant in the univariate LISA. The five Low-High townships are weak (one survives FDR): candidates for follow-up, perhaps where air assets are stretched or fighting is mostly small arms, which the counts cannot settle.

```{r}
#| label: bv-sens
# Airstrikes by State forces only (ACLED's interaction code for the first actor)
state_air <- conflict_ts |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(sub_event_type == "Air/drone strike", inter1 == "State forces") |>
  count(TS_PCODE, name = "state_air_n")
bv_in$state_air_n <- state_air$state_air_n[match(bv_in$TS_PCODE, state_air$TS_PCODE)] |> replace_na(0L)

bv_runs <- list(
  `Primary` = bv$bv_class,
  `Reversed: other events in township, airstrikes in neighbours` =
    run_bv(bv_in$other_n, bv_in$airstrike_n, nb_primary)$bv_class,
  `Battles only as y` = run_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in$battles_n, nb_primary)$bv_class,
  `State-force airstrikes only as x` = run_bv(bv_in$state_air_n, bv_in$other_n, nb_primary)$bv_class,
  `KNN k = 6 neighbours` = run_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in$other_n, nb_knn6)$bv_class,
  `Different seed (2026)` = run_bv(bv_in$airstrike_n, bv_in$other_n, nb_primary, seed = 2026)$bv_class,
  `log(1 + count) for both` = run_bv(log1p(bv_in$airstrike_n), log1p(bv_in$other_n), nb_primary)$bv_class)

imap_dfr(bv_runs, function(cls, label) {
  tibble(specification = label,
         significant = sum(cls != "Not significant"),
         same_class = paste0(round(100 * mean(cls == bv_runs$Primary)), "%"),
         high_high_kept = paste0(sum(cls == "High-High" & bv_runs$Primary == "High-High"), " of ",
                                 sum(bv_runs$Primary == "High-High")),
         low_low_kept = paste0(sum(cls == "Low-Low" & bv_runs$Primary == "Low-Low"), " of ",
                               sum(bv_runs$Primary == "Low-Low")),
         low_high_kept = paste0(sum(cls == "Low-High" & bv_runs$Primary == "Low-High"), " of ",
                                sum(bv_runs$Primary == "Low-High")),
         high_low = sum(cls == "High-Low"))
}) |> kable()
```

**What the sensitivity checks show.**

- **Clusters are stable, outliers are not.** At least `r min(map_int(bv_runs[-1], \(cls) sum(cls == "High-High" & bv_runs$Primary == "High-High")))` of the 29 High-High townships stay High-High in every alternative; only one Low-High township survives reversing the roles or logging the counts.
- **Direction matters.** With roles reversed (other events in the township, airstrikes around it), three Yangon townships become High-Low: North Okkalapa, Mingaladon and Hlaingtharya, with 140–194 other events each and almost no airstrikes nearby. This fits the urban fighting of 2021 (@sec-ehsa-results), though totals cannot show timing.
- **Who strikes.** *Air/drone strike* includes resistance drone attacks. State forces are first actor in `r scales::comma(sum(bv_in$state_air_n))` of `r scales::comma(sum(bv_in$airstrike_n))` strikes (`r round(100 * sum(bv_in$state_air_n) / sum(bv_in$airstrike_n))`%). Restricting $x$ to those keeps 24 of 29 High-High and all 47 Low-Low townships, so the Dry Zone result holds for the military's strikes.

# Emerging Hot Spot Analysis (EHSA) {#sec-ehsa}

The LMSA treats 57 months as one total, leaving two questions. Are the Dry Zone hot spots fixed, or did they appear, spread and fade? Were northern Shan and Rakhine, absent from the full-period maps, short-lived hot spots that the total dilutes? EHSA adds time: it computes Gi\* for every township in every quarter, then classifies each by the timing and persistence of its significant quarters [@esri_ehsa].

::: callout-tip
## Method card: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis

- **Question.** How has each township's hot or cold status changed across the 19 quarters?
- **Method.** (1) Quarterly Gi\* with the D3 neighbours plus self and the neighbours' values in the previous quarter (time lag k = 1, D7). (2) A Mann–Kendall test for a monotonic trend in each township's 19 Gi\* values [@mann1945; @kendall1975]. (3) A rule-based classification into one of 17 categories from the number, timing and sign of significant quarters and the trend [@esri_ehsa; @sfdep].
- **Null model.** Within each quarter, counts are spatially random; 999 permutations of that quarter's counts (@sec-ehsa-impl explains why).
- **Assumptions.** Gi\* is standardised within each quarter, so it measures *relative* concentration: a township can stop being hot because fighting rose elsewhere. Mann–Kendall assumes independence, which quarterly bins support (D7).
- **Edge handling.** As for Gi\*; the first quarter has no lag, so it uses spatial neighbours only.
- **Threshold.** 0.05 on the smaller one-sided permutation p-value and on Mann–Kendall (D8); 0.025 and 0.01 in @sec-ehsa-sens.
:::

The categories found in this study follow `sfdep`'s implementation of the Esri rules [@sfdep; @esri_ehsa]. "Significant" means p ≤ 0.05 in that quarter; "90%" means at least 18 of 19 quarters.

| Category | Rule (as implemented) |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| New hot spot | Significant hot in the final quarter only. |
| Consecutive hot spot | One unbroken run of significant hot quarters ending in the final quarter, nothing significant before it, under 90% of quarters hot. |
| Persistent hot spot | Significant hot in at least 90% of quarters, no significant trend. |
| Oscillating hot spot | Significant hot in the final quarter, significant cold in at least one earlier quarter. |
| Sporadic hot spot | Significant hot in some quarters, never significant cold, not covered above. |
| No pattern detected | No rule applies, including townships that were cold, then hot, then neither. |
| Sporadic / oscillating / consecutive / persistent cold spot | Mirror images of the hot rules. |

: EHSA categories that occur in this study

## Building the space-time cube {#sec-ehsa-cube}

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-cube
panel_quarter  <- read_rds("data/rds/panel_quarter.rds")
panel_month_an <- read_rds("data/rds/panel_month_an.rds")

# EHSA works on a copy of the analytical layer sorted by TS_PCODE.
# sfdep::emerging_hotspot_analysis() needs this (see the decision below).
ord      <- order(mmr_an$TS_PCODE)
ehsa_geo <- mmr_an[ord, ] |> select(TS_PCODE, ST, TS)

# Re-index a neighbour list after the rows have been re-ordered
reorder_nb <- function(nb, ord) {
  new_index <- order(ord)                     # old row -> new row
  out <- lapply(ord, function(i) sort(new_index[nb[[i]]]))
  class(out) <- "nb"
  attr(out, "region.id") <- attr(nb, "region.id")[ord]
  out
}
nb_ehsa      <- reorder_nb(nb_primary, ord)
nb_knn6_ehsa <- reorder_nb(nb_knn6, ord)
stopifnot(identical(card(nb_ehsa), card(nb_primary)[ord]),
          is.symmetric.nb(nb_ehsa, force = TRUE))

ehsa_geo$nb <- include_self(nb_ehsa)          # Gi*: township is its own neighbour
ehsa_geo$wt <- st_weights(ehsa_geo$nb)        # row-standardised (D4)

cube_q <- spacetime(panel_quarter, ehsa_geo,
                    .loc_col = "TS_PCODE", .time_col = "quarter")
is_spacetime_cube(cube_q)

# The same cube as township x time matrices, for the implementation below
cube_matrix <- function(panel, time_col) {
  m <- panel |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = TS_PCODE, names_from = all_of(time_col),
                values_from = conflict_n, names_sort = TRUE)
  out <- as.matrix(m[match(ehsa_geo$TS_PCODE, m$TS_PCODE), -1])
  rownames(out) <- ehsa_geo$TS_PCODE
  out
}
X_q <- cube_matrix(panel_quarter, "quarter")    # 329 x 19
X_m <- cube_matrix(panel_month_an, "month")     # 329 x 57 (sensitivity)
quarters <- sort(unique(panel_quarter$quarter))
q_labels <- paste0(year(quarters), " Q", quarter(quarters))
dim(X_q)
```

## Implementation: how significance is computed in each quarter {#sec-ehsa-impl}

Reading the source of `sfdep::emerging_hotspot_analysis()` (version 0.2.5) revealed three behaviours that matter here. Each is tested rather than assumed.

1.  **Results are matched to townships by position.** Townships are listed in geometry order but classified in alphabetical order of ID, so they line up only if the geometry is sorted by ID. This is not, so the cube above uses a sorted copy, and a check below confirms the alignment.
2.  **The permutation reference mixes all quarters.** Simulated neighbourhoods are drawn from all 6,251 township-quarters, while the observed Gi\* is standardised within its quarter. In a quiet quarter, draws from busier ones look large, so quiet townships look significantly cold, and the reverse in busy quarters. Q1 2021 has `r scales::comma(sum(X_q[, 1]))` events against a median of `r scales::comma(median(colSums(X_q)))` per quarter, so this matters.
3.  **One rule labels some cold spots as hot.** The "intensifying hot spot" rule counts significant quarters of *either* sign towards its 90% condition, so a persistent cold spot that is becoming less cold can be labelled an intensifying *hot* spot.

::: callout-important
## Decision: Gi\* as in `sfdep`, with each quarter tested against its own permutations

**Criteria.** (a) Gi\* must match `sfdep`'s exactly, keeping the course method. (b) The null must be spatial randomness *within a quarter*, which is what a hot spot in that quarter means. (c) Every label must belong to the right township and sign.

**Candidates.** (A) `sfdep::emerging_hotspot_analysis()` as is, on the sorted cube. (B) The same Gi\* and rules, with within-quarter permutations and the one rule corrected.
:::

The code runs (A) with 199 simulations, enough to show the effect, then implements (B) in a few lines reproducing `sfdep`'s Gi\* formula.

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-sfdep
set.seed(2025)
ehsa_sfdep <- emerging_hotspot_analysis(cube_q, .var = "conflict_n", k = 1,
                                        nb_col = "nb", wt_col = "wt",
                                        nsim = 199, threshold = 0.05,
                                        include_gi = TRUE)
# Gi* and p-values come back in time-then-township order
gi_sfdep <- matrix(attr(ehsa_sfdep, "gi_star")$gi_star, nrow = nrow(X_q))
p_sfdep  <- matrix(attr(ehsa_sfdep, "gi_star")$p_sim,   nrow = nrow(X_q))
```

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-impl
# Gi* for one quarter, as in sfdep's local_g_spt_calc(): the township and its
# neighbours now (W %*% x_t) plus the same neighbours one quarter earlier
# (W %*% x_lag), standardised by this quarter's mean and variance.
gi_slice <- function(W, x_t, x_lag = NULL) {
  n  <- length(x_t)
  lx <- as.numeric(W %*% x_t)
  Wi <- rowSums(W)
  S1 <- rowSums(W^2)
  if (!is.null(x_lag)) {
    lx <- lx + as.numeric(W %*% x_lag)
    Wi <- 2 * Wi
    S1 <- 2 * S1
  }
  xbar <- mean(x_t)
  s2   <- sum((x_t - xbar)^2) / n
  (lx - Wi * xbar) / sqrt(s2 * (n * S1 - Wi^2) / (n - 1))
}
gi_cube <- function(X, W) {
  sapply(seq_len(ncol(X)), function(t) gi_slice(W, X[, t], if (t > 1) X[, t - 1]))
}

# Permutation test with each quarter's counts shuffled within that quarter.
# p = smaller one-sided tail, as in sfdep (D5-D6).
# Quiet quarters have many identical neighbourhoods (for example all zeros), so many
# simulated Gi* values equal the observed one. Floating-point rounding differs between
# machines, so ties are compared with a small tolerance and counted as ties everywhere.
ehsa_gi <- function(X, nb, nsim = 999, seed = 2025, tol = 1e-9) {
  W   <- nb2mat(include_self(nb), style = "W")
  obs <- gi_cube(X, W)
  n_ge <- n_le <- matrix(0, nrow(X), ncol(X))
  set.seed(seed)
  for (s in seq_len(nsim)) {
    sim  <- gi_cube(apply(X, 2, sample), W)
    n_ge <- n_ge + (obs >= sim - tol)
    n_le <- n_le + (obs <= sim + tol)
  }
  list(gi = obs, p = pmin(n_ge + 1, n_le + 1) / (nsim + 1))
}

# sfdep's own classification rules, with the intensifying-hot-spot rule
# restricted to significant *hot* quarters, as in the Esri definition
ehsa_rules <- sfdep:::fxs
ehsa_rules[["intensifying hotspot"]] <- function(gs, sigs, n, tau, tau_p, threshold, ...) {
  (sum(sigs & gs > 0) / n >= 0.9) && sigs[n] && gs[n] > 0 && tau > 0 && tau_p < threshold
}
classify_ehsa <- function(gi, p, threshold = 0.05, rules = ehsa_rules) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(gi)), function(i) {
    gs   <- gi[i, ]
    sigs <- p[i, ] <= threshold
    mk   <- Kendall::MannKendall(gs)
    tau  <- as.numeric(mk$tau)
    tau_p <- as.numeric(mk$sl)
    hit <- vapply(rules, function(f) isTRUE(f(gs = gs, sigs = sigs, n = length(gs),
                                                tau = tau, tau_p = tau_p,
                                                threshold = threshold)), logical(1))
    tibble(tau = tau, mk_p = tau_p, classification = names(rules)[which(hit)[1]])
  })
}

fit_q <- ehsa_gi(X_q, nb_ehsa)
```

The checks below confirm that (B) differs from (A) only in the permutation reference.

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-validate
gi_ours <- gi_cube(X_q, nb2mat(include_self(nb_ehsa), style = "W"))
replayed <- classify_ehsa(gi_sfdep, p_sfdep, 0.05, rules = sfdep:::fxs)

tibble(
  check = c("Largest absolute difference between our Gi* and sfdep's (6,251 township-quarters)",
            "sfdep's location column is in the order of our sorted layer",
            "sfdep's Mann-Kendall tau equals ours for every township",
            "Our classifier, given sfdep's Gi*, p-values and rules, reproduces sfdep's labels"),
  result = c(format(max(abs(gi_ours - gi_sfdep)), digits = 2),
             identical(ehsa_sfdep$location, ehsa_geo$TS_PCODE),
             isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(ehsa_sfdep$tau), replayed$tau)),
             paste0(sum(replayed$classification == ehsa_sfdep$classification),
                    " of ", nrow(X_q)))) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ehsa-perm
#| fig-cap: "Number of townships flagged as significant hot or cold spots (p ≤ 0.05) in each quarter, under sfdep's pooled permutation reference (A) and under within-quarter permutation (B). The observed Gi* values are identical; only the reference distribution differs. The top panel shows the national number of armed-conflict events per quarter."
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-width: 8
perm_diag <- bind_rows(
  tibble(quarter = quarters, panel = "Armed-conflict events (national)",
         series = "Events", value = colSums(X_q)),
  tibble(quarter = quarters, panel = "Significant hot spots",
         series = "(A) sfdep, pooled", value = colSums(p_sfdep <= 0.05 & gi_sfdep > 0)),
  tibble(quarter = quarters, panel = "Significant hot spots",
         series = "(B) within-quarter", value = colSums(fit_q$p <= 0.05 & fit_q$gi > 0)),
  tibble(quarter = quarters, panel = "Significant cold spots",
         series = "(A) sfdep, pooled", value = colSums(p_sfdep <= 0.05 & gi_sfdep < 0)),
  tibble(quarter = quarters, panel = "Significant cold spots",
         series = "(B) within-quarter", value = colSums(fit_q$p <= 0.05 & fit_q$gi < 0))) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Armed-conflict events (national)",
                                          "Significant hot spots", "Significant cold spots")))

ggplot(perm_diag, aes(quarter, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Events" = "grey40", "(A) sfdep, pooled" = "#d95f02",
                                 "(B) within-quarter" = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-monthly-rule
# Effect of the corrected rule, shown on the monthly cube (used again in @sec-ehsa-sens)
fit_m     <- ehsa_gi(X_m, nb_ehsa)
m_fixed   <- classify_ehsa(fit_m$gi, fit_m$p, 0.05)
m_sfdep_r <- classify_ehsa(fit_m$gi, fit_m$p, 0.05, rules = sfdep:::fxs)

tibble(TS = ehsa_geo$TS, ST = ehsa_geo$ST,
       sfdep_rule = m_sfdep_r$classification,
       corrected_rule = m_fixed$classification,
       hot_months  = rowSums(fit_m$p <= 0.05 & fit_m$gi > 0),
       cold_months = rowSums(fit_m$p <= 0.05 & fit_m$gi < 0)) |>
  filter(sfdep_rule != corrected_rule) |>
  kable()
```

**Result.**

- **Gi\* and labels.** Our Gi\* matches `sfdep`'s to rounding error, the Mann–Kendall values match, and our classifier reproduces every `sfdep` label from `sfdep`'s inputs. With the sorted layer the labels line up; on the unsorted layer most are attached to the wrong townships.
- **Permutation reference.** In Q1 2021, the two months after the coup, (A) flags `r sum(p_sfdep[, 1] <= 0.05 & gi_sfdep[, 1] < 0)` townships as significant cold spots against `r sum(fit_q$p[, 1] <= 0.05 & fit_q$gi[, 1] < 0)` under (B) (@fig-ehsa-perm). Through 2021 (A) flags fewer hot spots, and in the busiest quarters (Q4 2023 to Q2 2024) more. Spurious early cold quarters followed by extra hot ones look exactly like "oscillating" or "intensifying" hot spots, biasing (A) towards escalation.
- **Classification rule.** On the monthly cube, the original rule labels the Wa and eastern Shan cold spots "intensifying hot spots" although none has a single significant hot month; the corrected rule labels them cold.

::: decision
**Decision.** (B) is the primary EHSA; (A)'s classes are kept for comparison.
:::

## Results {#sec-ehsa-results}

```{r}
#| label: ehsa-results
pretty_class <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace("oscilating", "oscillating") |>
    str_replace("hotspot", "hot spot") |>
    str_replace("coldspot", "cold spot") |>
    str_to_sentence()
}
family_of <- function(x) case_when(str_detect(x, "hot spot") ~ "Hot",
                                   str_detect(x, "cold spot") ~ "Cold", TRUE ~ "None")
sig_hot  <- fit_q$p <= 0.05 & fit_q$gi > 0
sig_cold <- fit_q$p <= 0.05 & fit_q$gi < 0

ehsa <- ehsa_geo |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(TS_PCODE, ST, TS) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(mmr_an) |> select(TS_PCODE, conflict_n), by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  bind_cols(classify_ehsa(fit_q$gi, fit_q$p, 0.05)) |>
  mutate(class       = pretty_class(classification),
         class_sfdep = pretty_class(ehsa_sfdep$classification),
         hot_q       = rowSums(sig_hot),
         cold_q      = rowSums(sig_cold),
         first_hot   = apply(sig_hot, 1, \(r) if (any(r)) q_labels[which(r)[1]] else NA),
         family      = family_of(class),
         # first quarter of the unbroken run of cold quarters that ends in Q3 2025
         cold_run_start = apply(sig_cold, 1, \(r) { k <- length(r); while (k > 1 && r[k - 1]) k <- k - 1; k }))

class_order <- c("New hot spot", "Consecutive hot spot", "Intensifying hot spot",
                 "Persistent hot spot", "Diminishing hot spot", "Oscillating hot spot",
                 "Historical hot spot", "Sporadic hot spot", "No pattern detected",
                 "Sporadic cold spot", "Historical cold spot", "Oscillating cold spot",
                 "Diminishing cold spot", "Persistent cold spot", "Intensifying cold spot",
                 "Consecutive cold spot", "New cold spot")

ehsa |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(townships        = n(),
            median_events    = median(conflict_n),
            median_hot_qtrs  = median(hot_q),
            median_cold_qtrs = median(cold_q),
            same_class_in_sfdep_A = paste0(round(100 * mean(class == class_sfdep)), "%")) |>
  arrange(match(class, class_order)) |>
  kable()
```

**Statistical conclusions.** Of 329 townships, `r sum(ehsa$family == "Hot")` have a hot spot class, `r sum(ehsa$family == "Cold")` a cold spot class and `r sum(ehsa$family == "None")` no pattern. None is a *persistent*, *intensifying* or *new* hot spot. The missing persistent class is informative: the most violent townships were not yet significant in the first two quarters of 2021, before the armed uprising, so they fall just short of the 90% rule (17 of 19 is 89.5%) and are *consecutive* instead. Mann–Kendall finds a significant upward Gi\* trend in `r sum(ehsa$tau > 0 & ehsa$mk_p < 0.05)` townships and a downward one in `r sum(ehsa$tau < 0 & ehsa$mk_p < 0.05)`.

The implementations agree on `r round(100 * mean(ehsa$class == ehsa$class_sfdep))`% of classes and `r round(100 * mean(ehsa$family == family_of(ehsa$class_sfdep)))`% of families. Disagreements stem from (A)'s extra 2021 cold quarters: consecutive hot spots become "oscillating" (`r sum(ehsa$class == "Consecutive hot spot" & ehsa$class_sfdep == "Oscillating hot spot")` of `r sum(ehsa$class == "Consecutive hot spot")`), sporadic hot spots not hot in the final quarter fall to "no pattern" (`r sum(ehsa$class == "Sporadic hot spot" & ehsa$class_sfdep == "No pattern detected")`), and consecutive cold spots become sporadic or persistent (`r sum(ehsa$class == "Consecutive cold spot" & ehsa$class_sfdep %in% c("Sporadic cold spot", "Persistent cold spot"))`). Under (A), many fronts would falsely appear to emerge from a cold 2021.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-ehsa
#| fig-cap: "Emerging hot spot classes of armed-conflict events, Q1 2021 – Q3 2025 (quarterly Gi* with Queen + island-bridge neighbours and a one-quarter time lag; 999 within-quarter permutations; threshold 0.05). Every class is defined by significant quarters (p ≤ 0.05); townships with no significant pattern are grey."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 9
ehsa_pal <- c(
  "New hot spot" = "#e7298a", "Consecutive hot spot" = "#b2182b",
  "Intensifying hot spot" = "#67001f", "Persistent hot spot" = "#d6604d",
  "Diminishing hot spot" = "#f4a582", "Oscillating hot spot" = "#fd8d3c",
  "Historical hot spot" = "#fee090", "Sporadic hot spot" = "#fcbba1",
  "No pattern detected" = "#eeeeee",
  "Sporadic cold spot" = "#deebf7", "Historical cold spot" = "#e0f3f8",
  "Oscillating cold spot" = "#80cdc1", "Diminishing cold spot" = "#abd9e9",
  "Persistent cold spot" = "#08519c", "Intensifying cold spot" = "#053061",
  "Consecutive cold spot" = "#6baed6", "New cold spot" = "#5e3c99",
  "Not analysed" = "#ffffff")

ehsa_levels <- c(intersect(class_order, unique(ehsa$class)), "Not analysed")

ehsa_map_data <- mmr_conflict |>
  select(TS_PCODE) |>
  left_join(select(ehsa, TS_PCODE, class), by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(class = factor(replace_na(class, "Not analysed"), levels = ehsa_levels))

tm_shape(ehsa_map_data) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "class",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = ehsa_pal[ehsa_levels]),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "EHSA class (threshold 0.05)",
                            position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
    col = "grey60", lwd = 0.2) +
  map_furniture() +
  tm_compass(type = "arrow", size = 2.5,
             position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, 100, 200), text.size = 0.6,
              position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"))
```

The hot and cold spot test was repeated for each of the 19 quarters, and every township is labelled by its history: reds are hot-spot histories, blues cold-spot histories, and grey means no clear history. Dark red marks *consecutive* hot spots, hot in an unbroken run up to the latest quarter: the Dry Zone core, its spread north and east of Mandalay, and Dawei and Palaw in Tanintharyi. Pale salmon marks *sporadic* hot spots, hot on and off, arcing from Chin and northern Sagaing through Kachin and down the eastern border through Kayah, Kayin and Mon to the far south. Six of the seven oscillating-cold townships (teal), briefly hot and then turned cold, are in the Kokang and Lashio area where Operation 1027 was fought. Dark blue marks *persistent* cold spots in the Wa and eastern Shan hills and part of the delta, Yangon is a block of consecutive cold spots, and Rakhine is almost entirely grey. Of 329 townships, 108 have a hot history and 166 a cold one. A label sums up 19 quarters in a few words and can hide a story: most of Rakhine is grey although it went from quiet to heavy fighting and back, which the timeline below shows in full.

@fig-map-ehsa shows the pattern but not the names. The interactive version below uses the same classes and colours: hover for township and state, click for class, event total and hot and cold quarters. It uses `tmap` `"view"` mode on Esri's light grey base map.

```{r}
#| label: view-on
#| echo: false
tmap_mode("view")
```

```{r}
tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
```

The same history map on a light base map: zoom in, hover over a township for its name and state, and click it for its class, total events and how many quarters it was hot or cold. Names make the pattern usable: the consecutive core can be read off directly as Yinmarbin, Pale, Salingyi, Myaing and their neighbours in the Dry Zone, and Kayin, Mon and Tanintharyi form the sporadic strip along the south-east. Clicking a grey township in Rakhine shows several hot and several cold quarters, a reminder that grey can hide a great deal of fighting. The map adds nothing after September 2025 or for individual events; the totals are recorded events, not casualties, and it is a reference tool for looking up a township, not new evidence.

Both maps show only the final label. The timeline shows how each label arose on the main fronts; each cell is one township-quarter.
